name: New Caledonia

findings.local_actor: OPT-NC (Office des Postes et Télécommunications de Nouvelle-Calédonie, owner)
findings.financier: OPT-NC own funds, French state subsidies, AFD loan
findings.summary: OPT-NC put the Gondwana-2 international cable to Fiji and the Picot-2 domestic loop into service in August 2022; Alcatel Submarine Networks built them under an April 2020 contract, final cost about XPF 4.68bn.
findings.analyst_inference: Controller convention (as GLP/GUF): NCL is coded as its own territory, so French-state, French-company and EU controllers are 'third'; only Caledonian actors such as OPT-NC are domestic. Equipment rule: ASN (France) is the system supplier, so pole third; owner OPT-NC is domestic. announced_value_usd is the USD figure stated by Developing Telecoms for the initial contract (XPF 4.474bn); the OPT-reported final cost of XPF 4.675bn was not converted, so verified_value_usd null. At commissioning the Île des Pins landing was still pending. Current operation not re-confirmed this run.

findings.local_actor: OPT-NC (sole mobile operator); Intelia (local integrator, exclusive Ericsson representative)
findings.summary: OPT-NC selected Intelia, Ericsson's exclusive local representative, for a three-year renewal worth about XPF 1.61bn covering 90 new 3G/LTE sites and the end of 2G; Intelia and Ericsson reportedly held about 20 OPT deals since 2010.
findings.analyst_inference: Corroborated set false: both trade-press items appeared within four days and almost certainly relay the same OPT-NC announcement, so they are not treated as independent, and they disagree on status (SubTel: selected/renewed; Developing Telecoms: planned renewal, value undisclosed). Ericsson (Sweden) is inferred as the RAN vendor from Intelia's exclusive-representative role; no source states the installed base is wholly Ericsson. EUR/XPF value not converted. Long-running relationship suggests an operational installed base (tier 5), but this run documents only the 2020 contract.

findings.summary: Nouméa's council authorised the mayor to sign a three-year framework contract, about XPF 30m a year, to supply and install 51 video-protection cameras; neither the awardee nor the camera manufacturer is named.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: no vendor or camera manufacturer is identified, and the system is not described as AI-enabled. Tier 2 rather than 3 because the deliberation authorises signature with an unnamed bidder, so no counterparty is documented. XPF value not converted.

facilities.null_reason: one search returned only aggregator listings of small Nouméa colocation sites (Citius, DSP DC1/DC2) and a government investment release not opened; no large data-centre or AI-campus project identified

silicon.null_reason: no dedicated search; no accelerator purchase or export-licence item surfaced in other searches

models.null_reason: one search returned only general Mistral/Microsoft news; no New Caledonia government partnership with a model provider and no local model found

research_gaps: Whether OPT-NC's current radio and core network is wholly Ericsson, and the vendor for its private 5G pilots for industry (2024).
Awardee and camera manufacturer of Nouméa's 2025 video-protection framework contract, and vendors of the Dumbéa licence-plate-reading cameras and other Grand Nouméa CCTV.

Contents of the New Caledonia government release on roughly XPF 9bn of private investment (gouv.nc PDF, not opened) for any data-centre component.
